key_insight: The paper reframes LLM routing as a single budget allocation problem, balancing resampling the current model against rerouting to another model to maximize expected correctness.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical serving strategy for cost-sensitive LLM systems, helping operators improve quality under fixed per-query budgets instead of relying on a single-shot router.
method: Formulate budget-aware test-time model selection with an imperfect verifier.
Use an online resample-or-reroute (RoR) policy driven by estimated marginal correctness per unit cost.
Allocate each query’s budget between resampling and rerouting based on recoverability asymmetry.
evidence_signal: Replay experiments on regenerated multi-draw correctness tensors from 11 open-weight models across 4 benchmarks show RoR improves the cost-quality Pareto front over several baselines, especially on the most heterogeneous task.
watch_item: The gains depend on verifier quality and can shrink substantially when the verifier is weak, so deployment needs careful verifier calibration and cost modeling.
paper_title: Resample or Reroute? Budget-Aware Test-Time Model Selection for Large Language Models
